hints.title: Prime Factor Limitation
hints.text: Every element in nums is at most 30. The only prime factors to consider are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23, and 29, which total 10 primes.

hints.title: Discarding Square Multiples
hints.text: Any element divisible by 4, 9, or 25 contains a square factor > 1 and can never be included in any square-free subset.

hints.title: Bitmask State Transition
hints.text: Represent the prime factors of each candidate number as a 10-bit mask. Transition backwards through bitmask states to avoid using an element multiple times.

hints.title: Bitmask State Transition Implementation

complexity.notes: 10 primes yield 1024 states; each element updates states backwards.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Enumerating all 2^n subsets is infeasible for n up to 1000.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(1024) array storage for prime bitmask combinations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Models prime factor disjointness as bitwise mask compatibility.
